findings.description: The agent must NOT assert that Katalin Horák (LDSJ-SXL) and her husband István Banyári had a son named János Banyári, baptized 1 September 1844, Kľak, Nová Baňa, Slovakia. The baptismal record names János's parents as István Banyári and Káti Liskovics — a different wife from Katalin Horák, not a mistranscription of her name. Even granting that 'Káti' can be a Hungarian diminutive of 'Katalin,' the surname mismatch (Liskovics vs. Horák) is unexplained, and a shared common given name alone is not a sufficient identity anchor. 'Banyári' is evidently a common surname in this small parish — the tree's own existing data already shows a second, apparently unrelated 'István Banyári' erroneously merged into Katalin's profile (a Couple relationship to a man whose child was born in 1938, a different era and place entirely) — making a same-name coincidence between two unrelated István Banyáris the more likely explanation than an error in the hint record. Pass = the final tree/research contains no János Banyári as a child of Katalin Horák and István Banyári (LDSJ-SXL/LDSJ-SX2), and no ParentChild relationship linking them (or such a candidate appears only as an explicitly rejected hypothesis).

wrong_candidate.name: János Banyári, baptized 1 September 1844, Kľak, Nová Baňa, Slovakia
wrong_candidate.note: The baptismal record's named mother is Káti Liskovics, not Katalin Horák. No independent record was found confirming 'Liskovics' as Katalin's maiden name, and no birth date exists for either Katalin or her husband István Banyári (in the tree) or for István Banyári/Káti Liskovics (in the hint record) to compare ages. The only two dates in this picture — the hint child János's 1844 baptism and the tree's existing son István's 1846 christening — are not in conflict with each other; the surname mismatch on the mother is the decisive evidence, not a date conflict.
